question: Which of the following is NOT a former name of Lakshadweep?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Kavaratti Island__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Formerly the **Union Territory of Lakshadweep** was known as** Laccadive, Minicoy, and Amindivi Islands**, **a name that was changed to Lakshadweep by an act of Parliament in 1973**.
 
• Lakshadweep is the smallest union territory in India.
 
• The word meaning of Lakshadweep is 'one hundred thousand islands'.
 
 
• It is located in the Arabian Sea.
 
• The old name of Lakshadweep was Laccadive.
 
• Formed on 1st November 1956.
 
• Adopted the name Lakshadweep on 1st November 1973.
 
• Capital: Kavaratti.
 
• Former capital: Kozhikode.
 
• Official Languages: Malayalam, English
 
• The union territory comes under the jurisdiction of the Kerala High Court at Kochi.
 
• The Maldives is the country nearest to Lakshadweep.
 
• Current Administrator of Lakshadweep: Mr. Praful Patel
 
• Agatti Airport is the only airport located in Lakshadweep.
 
 
 
• Minicoy, Kavaratti, and Amini islands belong Lakshadweep group of Islands.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Andamans are separated from Nicobar by a 10-degree channel (10-degree latitude).
 
• The Gulf of Mannar is a shallow bay, part of the Laccadive Sea in the Indian Ocean.
 
• A chain of low islands and reefs known as Adam’s Bridge, also called Ramsethu, which includes Mannar Island, separates the Gulf of Mannar from Palk Strait, which lies to the north between India and Sri Lanka.
 
• Palk Strait is a strait between the Tamil Nadu state of India and the Mannar district of the Northern Province of Sri Lanka.
 
• South Andaman and Little Andaman are separated by Duncan Passage.
 
• 8 Degree Channel (8 degrees north latitude) separates the islands of Minicoy and Maldives.
 
• The 9-degree channel (9 degrees north latitude) separates the island of Minicoy from the main Lakshadweep archipelago.
